input: Create a shared grocery list app with my partner

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The feature set drastically changes the complexity — a basic shared list vs. an app with categories, recipes, purchase history, or smart suggestions are very different builds.
Knowing whether this is just for two people or potentially more users affects the authentication and sharing model needed.
Whether this needs to be a mobile app, web app, or both determines the technology stack and platform to build on.
Budget and time availability determine whether to build from scratch, use a no-code tool, or adapt an existing solution like a shared notes app.
The user's technical skill level determines whether to recommend coding it, using a no-code platform, or configuring an existing app — a completely different path.
Understanding what 'done well' looks like — e.g. real-time sync, offline support, notifications — sets the quality bar and shapes priorities.
Knowing the immediate next action preference (start coding, research tools, sketch a design) determines where the plan should begin.

gold.taskTitle: Build a shared grocery list app with partner
gold.taskDescription: Create a collaborative grocery list application that both the user and their partner can access and manage together.

questions.title: Which features must the app include at launch?
questions.description: Identify the core feature set — e.g. add/remove items, check off items, categories, quantity tracking, or recipe integration — to define the scope of the build.

questions.title: Will only you and your partner use this app?
questions.description: Clarify whether the app is strictly for two users or needs to support additional people like housemates or family members, which affects the sharing and permissions model.

questions.title: Should this work as a mobile app, web app, or both?
questions.description: Determine the target platform so the right technology stack or tool can be chosen from the start.

questions.title: What is your budget and time available for this project?
questions.description: Understand any hard limits on money and hours to decide between building from scratch, using a no-code tool, or repurposing an existing app.

questions.title: How comfortable are you with writing code?
questions.description: Gauge technical skill level to recommend the most appropriate approach — custom development, a no-code platform, or configuring an existing solution.

questions.title: What would make this app feel like a clear success to you?
questions.description: Pin down the quality bar — such as real-time sync between devices, offline access, push notifications, or a clean design — to set the right priorities.

questions.title: Do you want to start building, researching tools, or designing first?
questions.description: Identify the preferred immediate next action so the plan can begin at the right starting point for the user.
